name: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd_DVR
title: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd_DVR - 570004 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue about flat near Rs 1,500 crore but EBITDA fell on lost fixed-cost absorption; NCD repayments of about Rs 680 crore due in FY27 hinge on refinancing and internal accruals.

I think as we go along, as we move forward for September, as the market improves, that something would be seriously looked at.

summary.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~2.5% to about Rs 1,500 crore, EBITDA margin dropped ~2 pts, and adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell on lower standalone India fixed-cost absorption, weaker Hi-Tech volumes and negative forex, while plastics margin improved. Management said April was weak but May, June and July improved, and it expects a stronger second half. Rs 164 crore of EBITDA was converted to cash at about 78%, and net working capital days fell to 183 from 210 a year ago. Rs 680-690 crore of NCDs fall due in September (about Rs 230 crore) and March; management says these will be met from internal cash flow with refinancing and other options in progress.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Revenue down about 22% YoY; retail down 17% (MIS down 16% to Rs 368 crore, tissue culture down 10%) and project down 63%. Margin fell from 16.6% to 14.4%; management guides to double-digit growth for FY27.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY, with overseas plastics revenue up about 40%. EBITDA margin improved to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on beverages (about Rs 60 crore in the quarter) and overseas sales; EBITDA lower on seasonality and margin down about 3 pts.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to recover the Q1 EBITDA shortfall in H2 FY27 and to do better than last year at PAT level for the full year.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.
Hi-Tech expected to deliver double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with solar pump billing to pick up from September.
Government receivables target: about Rs 422 crore for FY27 (Rs 60 crore collected in Q1, minimum Rs 380 crore in the remaining nine months).
Dividends expected from next year (FY28) as standalone India business generates positive cash flow.
Tamil Nadu land monetisation expected to be delivered in the current quarter, per management.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started, using agri-waste (corn cob, cotton stalk, mango stones); impact on numbers expected from next fiscal.
Coffee Board first orders received; revenue has started.
Large Pune water-supply project still needs triple-digit billing; other projects about 98-99% complete with about Rs 40-50 crore billing left.
About 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over the next two to three years; management says O&M spend is light.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; management says most increases were passed on to customers, and customers deferred purchases until prices ease.
Delayed monsoon onset in June hit farm purchases; July rainfall was good and July revenue grew versus April-June.
Dam levels at about 67% of capacity; management hopes for 85% by monsoon end, which it sees as positive for Rabi and next summer.
Company chose not to pursue government-subsidy micro-irrigation business that would have needed longer receivables; management says about Rs 50-60 crore more sales were possible.
Institutional demand for larger-diameter pipes is being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt falls due and what are the repayment options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NCDs of about Rs 680-690 crore fall due (about Rs 230 crore in September, rest in March). Options listed: internal accruals (primary), legacy receivable collection, surplus land monetisation and refinancing; term sheets are in hand.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivable will be collected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about Rs 422 crore for FY27, with Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and at least Rs 380 crore expected in the remaining nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material write-offs are expected; provisions were made in earlier review and the remaining good receivables will be collected.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone working capital requirements higher than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to long-tail legacy project receivables and state-government orders on behalf of farmers, which are paid in six months to one year. Expects improvement from FY28 once project receivables clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the delay in the food business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Market valuations fell over the past year, so merchant bankers advised waiting; the total issue, including PE exit and primary funds, was expected at about Rs 1,000 crore. Management expects action from September if markets improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hi-Tech margin down and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% on lower volumes. Management said a full-year standalone margin of about 14% and consolidated 12-13% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the receivables are over 180 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 1,100 crore is above 180 days (about Rs 300 crore of farmer-order receivables plus Rs 800-900 crore of government receivables), roughly 55% of the Rs 1,975 crore net receivables.

risks_watch: Debt service: about Rs 230 crore of NCDs due in September; refinancing and asset monetisation timelines remain unconfirmed.
Recovery of Rs 380 crore of legacy government receivables in nine months; about 55% of net receivables (about Rs 1,100 crore) are above 180 days.
Polymer price volatility and oil/geopolitical risk could delay customer purchases.
Monsoon progress in August-September, which management says is critical for H2 volumes.
Food business IPO and PE exit timing with no confirmed date; Tamil Nadu land sale repeatedly delayed.
Whether the H2 margin catch-up materialises; Q1 adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore.
